**Start with what the product must answer.** A document assistant should answer questions from the user's permitted documents and show where each factual claim came from. It is not enough to produce a plausible paragraph. The system must find the right evidence, interpret it correctly, and avoid showing information the user cannot access.

**Walk one question through the system.** A user uploads an annual report and asks, “Why did operating costs rise?” First extract text, tables, page numbers, and section structure. Split the report into searchable pieces while retaining links to the original pages. At question time, search those pieces, rerank the shortlist, and give the strongest evidence to the language model. The answer should cite the pages explaining the cost drivers, not merely a page containing the word “cost.” [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401)

**Separate three kinds of failure.** If the relevant passage never enters the shortlist, retrieval failed. If it is present but the model misreads the number or period, generation failed. If the answer is correct but points to an unrelated page, citation grounding failed. Measuring only final answer fluency hides all three.

**Why permissions belong before generation.** Asking the model to ignore unauthorized text is weaker than never retrieving that text for the user. Store access metadata with chunks and enforce it in retrieval and final evidence selection. Derived summaries and caches also need the same access scope; otherwise a previously authorized result can leak later.

Begin with a small evaluated corpus, explicit abstention when evidence is missing, and a repeatable set of questions with answer-bearing passages. Scale ingestion and indexing only after the basic evidence path works. The design below adds the operational details needed for updates, retries, and multi-tenant use.

**Technical details and references.**

Start with tenant isolation and retrieval quality as separate requirements. Store immutable document versions, page/slide coordinates, extraction quality, tenant ID, and ACL/version metadata. Ingestion runs through a durable queue into malware scanning, OCR/layout extraction, table-aware chunking, embedding, and lexical indexing; failed documents enter a retry/dead-letter workflow. Stable chunk IDs make updates and deletions idempotent.

At query time authenticate the user and resolve current groups. Apply tenant and permission filters inside BOTH lexical and vector retrieval; do not retrieve across tenants and hope the final prompt filters secrets. Fuse authorized candidates with RRF, score(d)=Σ1/(c+rank(d)), rerank a bounded shortlist, and assemble cited context. Recheck authorization before returning source content, including when cached results are used. ACL revocation must invalidate relevant cache entries or make their permission versions stale; fail closed if authorization is unavailable.

For an illustrative sizing estimate, 100 million documents × 10 chunks × 768 dimensions × 2 bytes is 1.536 TB of raw vectors before replicas, indexes, metadata, or document storage. Shard primarily by tenant/placement policy, with large tenants partitioned further. Measure authorized recall@k, grounded answer correctness, permission-leak tests, freshness lag, and p95 latency. Hybrid retrieval improves coverage but increases index synchronization work; an LLM is never the authorization boundary.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** Measure retrieval recall separately from grounded answer correctness. A useful groundedness quantity is supported factual claims divided by checked factual claims, but high groundedness alone can reward evasive answers. Pair it with task completion, citation localization, ACL correctness, and deletion propagation. Budget p95 latency across retrieval, reranking, and generation using measured joint behavior. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval) and [2](https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/users-roles/cluster-or-deployment-auth/controlling-access-at-document-field-level).
